questions.q: List the characteristics of living beings.
questions.a: Growth, respiration, nutrition, response to stimuli, excretion and reproduction.

questions.q: Why is a moving bus not living?
questions.a: It cannot grow, feed, respire or reproduce by itself.

questions.q: How do plants show response to stimuli?
questions.a: Shoots bend toward light; mimosa leaves fold on touch.
A seed sprouting into a seedling when it gets air, water and warmth.

questions.q: Name the conditions needed for germination.
questions.a: Air (oxygen), water and warmth - light is not needed for most seeds.

questions.q: What comes out first from a germinating seed?
questions.a: The baby root (radicle), which grows downward, then the shoot.

concepts.title: Life Cycles of Plants and Animals

questions.a: The stages of an organism's life from birth to reproduction of the next generation.

questions.q: Name the stages of a butterfly's life cycle.
Do all animals have the same life cycle stages?
questions.a: No - mammals grow young directly; insects and frogs change form (metamorphosis).

questions.q: Why were cars and clouds once puzzling - living or not?
questions.a: They move and change like living things, so early thinkers wondered; but they cannot grow or reproduce.

questions.q: Name one thing that grows but is not living.
questions.a: A cloud grows (snow crystals) - but has no life processes of its own.

questions.q: What settles the question of whether something is living?
questions.a: Whether it shows all life processes - nutrition, respiration, growth, response and reproduction.
